## Zoning Evaluation — 1218 W George St, Chicago, IL
**PIN:** 14291230290000 | **Parcel resolution:** Authoritative (county address records)

---

### 1. Zoning District Currently in Effect

This parcel is zoned **RT-4** (Residential Two-Flat, Townhouse and Multi-Unit District), per ordinance **23082T1**. You can verify this on the official Chicago Zoning Map: [gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

### 2. Is Residential Use Allowed?

**Yes — residential is the primary permitted use** in the RT-4 district. RT-4 is a residential district designed for two-flats, townhouses, and multi-unit buildings. The existing structure is recorded as a 3-unit, 2-story building (built 1882), consistent with typical RT-4 development. Residential use is governed broadly by Chapter 17-2 of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance.

---

### 3. Key Bulk and Density Standards

The context did not retrieve the RT-4 zone definition directly (`zone_definition` is null), so the specific FAR, height limit, and lot-area-per-unit figures for RT-4 are **not confirmed from the retrieved code text**. I can state what the code framework establishes and what applies generally:

- **Minimum Lot Area per Dwelling Unit:** All R-district development is subject to minimum lot-area-per-unit standards under [2]. For the RT-4 district specifically, these figures are set in the § 17-2-0303 table, but the precise RT-4 per-unit figure was not returned in the retrieved code chunk — you should verify in § 17-2-0303-A directly.
- **RS3 Exemption (for reference):** [2] notes that in RS3 districts the minimum lot area per unit may be reduced to 1,500 sq ft under specific block-predominance conditions — this exemption is **RS3-specific** and does not automatically apply to RT-4.
- **Setbacks:** [5] establishes that no side setbacks are required in B and C districts; RT-4 is an R district, so the R-district setback rules under § 17-2-0305 (front) and § 17-2-0306 (rear) apply. Off-street parking in RT districts is prohibited in side setbacks and within 20 feet of the front property line per [3].
- **FAR and Maximum Height:** These are set in the § 17-2-0400 table for RT districts. The zone definition was not retrieved — **you must verify the specific RT-4 FAR and height caps in § 17-2-0400 directly** or via the Chicago Zoning Ordinance portal at [municode.com](https://www.municode.com/library/il/chicago).

> **What I could not determine:** The exact FAR, maximum building height, and the precise minimum lot area per unit for RT-4 were not in the retrieved code text. Do not rely on the generic framework above for design or permitting decisions without confirming the RT-4 row in the § 17-2-0303-A and § 17-2-0400 tables.

---

### 4. Overlays and Special Designations

The parcel carries **three regulatory overlays** and several negative determinations:

- **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA):** This parcel is in a CTA TOD overlay. The nearest CTA rail station is **Wellington (Brown/Purple Lines)**, approximately 0.34 miles away. See parking implications in item 5 below.
- **ADU Eligible Area:** This parcel falls within an Additional Dwelling Unit (ADU)-Allowed area under [1]. This means coach houses or conversion units may be permittable on this lot, subject to limitations in [1] (§ 17-7-0573) and pre-certification through the Department of Housing per § 17-7-0572 / § 2-44-106(g). Since the base zoning is RT-4 (not RS), confirm with the Department of Housing whether the specific ADU-allowed RS-area rules apply or whether a different ADU pathway governs.
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone:** The parcel is in an ARO zone. Residential projects that trigger the ARO (generally 10+ units) must provide affordable units or pay an in-lieu fee. The Lake View community area already has 20 ARO projects totaling 432 affordable units, including senior and supportive housing. Contact the Dept. of Housing for project-specific ARO obligations.
- **No Planned Development:** The parcel is not within a Planned Development.
- **No Landmark or Historic District:** Not a landmark building, not in a landmark district, not in a historic district, not on the National Register of Historic Places — no Commission on Chicago Landmarks review required for alterations.
- **No Lakefront Protection Overlay.**
- **No Pedestrian Street designation.**
- **No Special Service Area (SSA).**
- **No Special District or PMD.**
- **Flood Zone X** — FEMA designation "Area of Minimal Flood Hazard." Not a Special Flood Hazard Area; flood insurance is not federally required.
- **No brownfield sites nearby** — no environmental due diligence flags from the city data.

---

### 5. Parking Requirement and Transit-Related Reduction

Because this parcel is in the CTA TOD overlay, it qualifies for parking relief under § 17-10-0102-B. Specifically, **the minimum parking requirement may be reduced by up to 100%** — meaning no off-street parking spaces are required for this parcel. Note that this is parking *minimum* relief only; it is **not** a density, FAR, or height bonus. Per the applicable code, those bonuses apply only in "dash-3" districts (e.g., B1-3, B2-3, C1-3, DX-3) — RT-4 is **not** eligible for such bonuses.

If parking is provided regardless, it must comply with location rules under [3]: off-street parking for residential uses must be on the same zoning lot as the dwelling units served, and is prohibited in side setbacks or within 20 feet of the front property line.

**To verify:** Review § 17-10-0102-B in the Chicago Zoning Ordinance and confirm the TOD overlay boundary includes this parcel via the zoning map linked above.

---

### 6. Has the Zoning Changed Recently?

The current RT-4 designation is tied to ordinance **23082T1**, which appears to be a relatively recent ordinance number (the "23" prefix suggests 2023). This indicates the RT-4 designation may have been affirmed or amended in 2023. However, the context does not include a zoning change history, so I **cannot confirm the prior zoning classification or the nature of the 2023 action** (e.g., whether it was a reclassification or a routine map correction).

**To verify zoning history:**
- Search the Chicago City Clerk's legislative records at [chicityclerk.com](https://www.chicityclerk.com) using ordinance number 23082T1.
- Cross-reference with the Chicago Department of Planning and Development's zoning map and amendment records.

---

### Additional Context: Property and Neighborhood

The property is a **3-unit, 2-story, frame-construction building** (2,350 sq ft building on a 3,075 sq ft lot, built 1882) with a full basement and 2-car garage. Estimated 2024 property tax is **~$17,479/year**, primarily to the Board of Education ($9,589), City of Chicago ($4,265), and Cook County ($1,031). The property has a **standard tax class (211)** with no special Cook County incentive reduction.

The parcel sits within the **"Red and Purple Modernization Phase One" TIF district** (est. 2016, expiring 2052) — TIF increment financing may be available for qualifying projects; consult the Dept. of Planning and Development.
